findings.title: Any task notification suppresses all unbacked-action signals
findings.what: The parser sets taskNotificationSeen for any user content containing a task-notification tag, then initializes the session-wide hasVerificationEvidence flag from that boolean. Consequently, an unrelated notification such as a completed documentation task makes a later unsupported claim like “I ran the tests” appear backed, yielding unbackedClaimCount=0 without a matching verification command or result. This makes the emitted detector evidence non-reproducible from the claimed action.
findings.fix: Do not promote a bare session-wide notification to generic verification evidence. Require a resolved, relevant verification command/result, or parse and correlate notification identity/type to the specific action claim before treating it as backing evidence.
findings.acceptance: Add a regression fixture containing only an unrelated task-notification followed by “I ran the tests and they pass”; assert unbackedClaimCount is 1. Retain a fixture with a successful verification Bash tool_use/tool_result and assert the corresponding claim remains backed with count 0.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 174-175 accept notification presence without inspecting its task, outcome, or relationship to a claim; line 188 makes that boolean global evidence, and lines 245-248 suppress every deferred action claim whenever it is true. The existing background-completion test at src/lib/parse-deceit-signals.test.ts:67 includes both a notification and a successful Bash result, so it does not disprove the notification-only false negative.
